title: Ballistic: Ecks vs. Sever
full_review:
So explosively violent is "Ballistic: Ecks vs. Sever" (Warner Bros.) that stars Antonio Banderas and Lucy Liu are almost beside the point. They are mere instruments of destruction in this trashy tale of vengeance-motivated kidnapping and killing.

The narrative, in fact, is murky and confusing, especially concerning Liu's murderous character, agent-turned-kidnapper Sever, who repeatedly goes up against a slew of armed men surrounding her, and, with flying fists and lethal limbs, comes out unscathed. Such is the nonsensical level of this movie.

Another character believes his wife was murdered, just as she conveniently believes he was murdered, so now she is married to the villain of the piece, and harboring a far-too-easy-to-guess secret about her child.

The director, who uses the single name Kaos, an abbreviated form of his Thai surname, orchestrates a nearly nonstop barrage of shootouts, car bombings and utter mayhem which suggest that violence is simply exciting entertainment. And then we are to believe that the murderous Sever is actually good, her kidnapping of a child and multiple shootings all justified by her need to avenge her own son's death, which she accomplishes with icy determination.

Ex-FBI agent Ecks (Banderas) is on her tail but eventually they learn they have a common enemy (Gregg Henry). Punchy, overloud music underscores the brutality of the hand-to-hand fighting and extended shootouts -- which are the true focus of the story, not the bogus emotions that are ridiculous to watch. With stick-figure characters and its rationalization of homicidal violence, the misleadingly titled "Ballistic: Ecks vs. Sever" is a total time-waster.

Because of excessive violence and brief rough language, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
